cases.sentence: В Гвоздеве болото дупелиное по сю сторону, а за Гвоздевым идут чудные ___, и дупеля бывают.
cases.explain: «бекасиные болота» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Our plan is this. Now we’re driving to Gvozdyov. In Gvozdyov there’s a grouse marsh on this side, and beyond Gvozdyov come some magnificent snipe marshes where there are grouse too. It’s hot now, and we’ll get there—it’s fifteen miles or so—towards evening and have some evening shooting; we’ll spend the night there and go on tomorrow to the bigger moors.”

cases.sentence: Теперь жарко, и мы к вечеру (двадцать верст) приедем и возьмем вечернее поле; переночуем, а уже завтра в ___.
cases.explain: «большие болота» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Our plan is this. Now we’re driving to Gvozdyov. In Gvozdyov there’s a grouse marsh on this side, and beyond Gvozdyov come some magnificent snipe marshes where there are grouse too. It’s hot now, and we’ll get there—it’s fifteen miles or so—towards evening and have some evening shooting; we’ll spend the night there and go on tomorrow to the bigger moors.”

cases.sentence: Поравнявшись с ___, Левин хотел проехать мимо, но опытный охотничий глаз Степана Аркадьича тотчас же рассмотрел видную с дороги мочежину.
cases.explain: «маленьким болотцем» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Levin would himself have liked to go into these little places, but they were near home; he could shoot them over any time, and they were only little places—there would hardly be room for three to shoot. And so, with some insincerity, he said that he doubted there being anything to shoot. When they reached a little marsh Levin would have driven by, but Stepan Arkadyevitch, with the experienced eye of a sportsman, at once detected reeds visible from the road.

cases.explain: «другой собаки» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Really, there’s not room. Laska, back, Laska! You won’t want another dog, will you?”

cases.sentence: Когда они подъехали ко ___, которое было довольно велико и должно было взять много времени, Левин уговаривал не выходить.
cases.explain: «второму болоту» — after the preposition «ко», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: When they reached the second marsh, which was fairly large, and would inevitably take some time to shoot over, Levin tried to persuade them to pass it by. But Veslovsky again overpersuaded him. Again, as the marsh was narrow, Levin, like a good host, remained with the carriage.

cases.sentence: Опять, так как болото было узко, Левин, как ___, остался у экипажей.
cases.explain: «гостеприимный хозяин» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: When they reached the second marsh, which was fairly large, and would inevitably take some time to shoot over, Levin tried to persuade them to pass it by. But Veslovsky again overpersuaded him. Again, as the marsh was narrow, Levin, like a good host, remained with the carriage.

cases.sentence: Весловский сделал промах, и дупель пересел в ___.
cases.explain: «некошеный луг» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Krak made straight for some clumps of sedge. Vassenka Veslovsky was the first to run after the dog. Before Stepan Arkadyevitch had time to come up, a grouse flew out. Veslovsky missed it and it flew into an unmown meadow. This grouse was left for Veslovsky to follow up. Krak found it again and pointed, and Veslovsky shot it and went back to the carriage. “Now you go and I’ll stay with the horses,” he said.

cases.sentence: Маленькая ___ только на мгновенье развлекла ее.
cases.explain: «болотная птичка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: As she came nearer and nearer to the familiar breeding places there was more and more earnestness in Laska’s exploration. A little marsh bird did not divert her attention for more than an instant. She made one circuit round the clump of reeds, was beginning a second, and suddenly quivered with excitement and became motionless.

cases.sentence: Он слышал шаги Степана Аркадьича, принимая их за ___ лошадей, слышал хрупкий звук оторвавшегося с кореньями угла кочки, на которую он наступил, принимая этот звук за полет дупеля.
cases.explain: «дальний топот» — after the preposition «с», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Come, come, Stiva!” shouted Levin, feeling his heart beginning to beat more violently; and all of a sudden, as though some sort of shutter had been drawn back from his straining ears, all sounds, confused but loud, began to beat on his hearing, losing all sense of distance. He heard the steps of Stepan Arkadyevitch, mistaking them for the tramp of the horses in the distance; he heard the brittle sound of the twigs on which he had trodden, taking this sound for the flying of a grouse. He heard too, not far behind him, a splashing in the water, which he could not explain to himself.
